stem:
Soham's data are $4$, $6$, and $8$, so the mean is $6$. He multiplies every value by $3$.

What happens to the mean?

options.text: Multiply the mean by $3$ even if only one of the three values were multiplied by $3$.
Say that the new mean is what creates the factor $3$ on each value.
The new mean is $6\times 3=18$, because every value was multiplied by $3$.
Use the same $\times 3$ mean rule when every value is instead increased by $3$.

teacher.key_rationale: If every value is multiplied by a fixed number, the mean is multiplied by that same number: $6\times 3=18$. Applying the rule when only one value changes, reversing mean and factor, or swapping multiply for add all leave that scaling.
